title: feat: allow installing a specific release tag via --update --tag
body:
## Why

I maintain [decky-apps-manager](https://github.com/moi952/decky-apps-manager), a Decky Loader plugin that manages Flatpak apps and Gear Lever-tracked AppImages from the Steam Deck's Quick Access Menu. Users asked for the ability to switch an installed AppImage to a specific release instead of always being stuck on whatever `--update` resolves as latest — useful when a new version breaks something and you want to go back, or just to try a pre-release.

There's currently no way to do this through the CLI: `--update` always installs whatever the configured update manager resolves as "latest" (`/releases/latest`, or the newest non-draft when pre-releases are allowed) — there's no way to target an arbitrary tag.

We initially worked around this entirely from outside Gear Lever: downloading the asset for a chosen release ourselves and overwriting the tracked AppImage file directly. That turned out to be the wrong approach — Gear Lever's own displayed version doesn't come from re-reading the AppImage's own bytes, it's the `X-AppImage-Version` key baked into the `.desktop` file at `install_file()` time. Swapping the file underneath Gear Lever without going through its own install pipeline left that `.desktop` file stale, so both our plugin and Gear Lever's own app kept reporting the *previous* version — while `is_update_available()` (which does compare real file content) correctly noticed a mismatch, producing a confusing "app is at version X, but an update is available" even right after switching to an older release.

Rather than keep working around Gear Lever's internals from the outside, it seemed better to add real support for this here, so the fix is correct for every consumer (the GTK app included), not just a plugin-side hack.

## What this adds

- `GithubUpdater.list_available_versions()`: every non-draft release whose assets include one matching the app's already-configured `repo_filename` pattern.
- `GithubUpdater.fetch_target_asset()` / `download()` accept an optional `target_tag`, resolved via GitHub's `/releases/tags/<tag>` endpoint instead of `/latest` when given.
- CLI: a new `--list-versions <file_path>` command, and `--update` gains a `--tag <tag>` option.

Scoped to `GithubUpdater` for now to keep this reviewable — GitLab/Codeberg/Forgejo could get the same treatment as a follow-up, they share basically the same shape (`repo`/`repo_url` + `repo_filename`, releases API with a tag-lookup endpoint).

## Compatibility

- `UpdateManager.download()`'s abstract signature gained `target_tag: Optional[str] = None`; every other manager (`GitlabUpdater`, `CodebergUpdater`, `ForgejoUpdater`, `StaticFileUpdater`, `FTPUpdater`) got the same optional, currently-unused parameter added to keep the ABC contract consistent — no behavior change for any of them.
- `--update --tag` is rejected outright for a non-GitHub update source, and can't be combined with `--all`.
- Everything is additive and optional — plain `--update` (no `--tag`) behaves exactly as before.

title: fix: expose real available_version in --list-updates --json instead of hardcoded null
body:
## Context
`--list-updates --json` always reported `"available_version": null`, even when an update was genuinely found. None of the Git-hosting updaters (Github/Gitlab/Codeberg/Forgejo) track a version number to decide whether an update exists — they compare a zsync hash, an asset digest, or a raw file size — so nothing ever filled this field in.

## Fix
Each of those four updaters already fetches the matching release via its host's API during fetch_target_asset(). This just keeps the release's tag_name around (UpdateManager._last_available_version) and exposes it through a small get_available_version() helper, which Cli._make_app_json now reads instead of the hardcoded null.

No extra network calls — reuses data already fetched for the existing update check.

## Tested
Built locally with flatpak-builder --run against two real installed AppImages with GitHub update sources configured; `--list-updates --json` now reports a real tag (e.g. "2.4.0-beta.5") instead of null for the one with an actual update pending.

title: refresh_data reads the version from the installed .desktop, so a replaced AppImage keeps showing the old version
body:
If an integrated AppImage gets replaced in place by a newer build, Gear Lever keeps showing the version it recorded when the app was first integrated. The file on disk moves forward, the version in Gear Lever stays put.

I noticed it with Mendeley Reference Manager. Gear Lever listed 2.138.0.324, while the AppImage it points at was 2.148.0.341:

```sh
./mendeley_reference_manager.appimage --appimage-extract '*.desktop'
grep X-AppImage-Version squashfs-root/*.desktop
# X-AppImage-Version=2.148.0.341
```

## Cause

`refresh_data` in `src/providers/AppImageProvider.py`, lines 197 to 200 on master (a2917f2, 4.6.2):

```python
extracted = self._load_appimage_metadata(el)
if extracted.desktop_entry:
    el.name = extracted.desktop_entry.getName()
    el.version = el.desktop_entry.get('X-AppImage-Version')
```

The name is read from `extracted.desktop_entry`, which `_load_appimage_metadata` pulls out of the AppImage itself. The version is read from `el.desktop_entry`, which line 582 builds from `el.desktop_file_path`, the installed entry under `~/.local/share/applications`. Gear Lever writes that file when it integrates or updates an app, so it holds the version from that moment and nothing refreshes it afterwards.

## What it affects

The version toggle on the app details page, the installed apps list, and `gearlever --list-installed`, including the `--json` output documented in the README.

Update detection is not affected. None of the updaters read `el.version` in `is_update_available`. They compare the remote hash or the remote byte size against the local file, so I saw no spurious update prompts because of this.

## Possible fix

```python
el.version = extracted.desktop_entry.get('X-AppImage-Version')
```

or route it through `_get_app_version(extracted)` to keep the md5 fallback.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Integrate an AppImage through Gear Lever.
2. Replace the file in place with a newer build of the same app, either by hand or by letting the app update itself.
3. Reopen Gear Lever. The old version is still shown, while the `.desktop` inside the AppImage carries the new one.

## Environment

```
                Os= Fedora Linux 44 (Workstation Edition)
            Kernel= 7.1.7-cachyos1.fc44.x86_64
Desktop Enviroment= KDE plasmashell 6.7.4
        Compositor= wayland
           flatpak= Flatpak 1.18.1
        Gear Lever= 4.6.2
```

title: [Feature] Optional grid view for integrated AppImages
body:
Hi, first of all, thanks for Gear Lever, it’s been really useful for managing AppImages.

I wanted to suggest a feature that could make the main window even nicer to use: an optional **grid view** for integrated AppImages.

The current list view works well, especially for management tasks like checking details, versions, and available actions. But for users with a lot of AppImages, a grid or card-style layout could make browsing much quicker and more intuitive, especially when identifying apps by their icons.

What I had in mind is a simple view toggle in the main window:
- List view, as the current default
- Grid view, as an optional alternative

In grid view, each app card could show:
- App icon
- App name
- Version or update status
- Quick actions like launch, update, and remove, or possibly a context menu instead

I think this could help with:
- Faster visual navigation when managing many AppImages
- Better use of space on larger screens
- A more natural, launcher-like browsing experience, while still keeping Gear Lever focused as a manager

Of course, the current list workflow would remain unchanged if this were added as an optional toggle.

I’d also be happy to help with this feature and start working on a pull request, if this sounds like a direction that would fit the project. I can also prepare a first UI/UX mockup or proposal before implementation if that would be helpful.

title: Add option to install AppImages into their own dedicated folder
body:
Closes #397
 
Adds the option to install an AppImage into its own dedicated subfolder instead of the shared default AppImages folder. This is useful for AppImages that run in portable mode and expect to keep their data next to themselves, rather than mixed in with every other installed app.
 
**What's new:**
 
- A new "Install in its own folder" checkbox when integrating a single AppImage.
- The same option available when integrating multiple AppImages at once.
- A matching `--own-folder` flag for the CLI (`gearlever --integrate <file> --own-folder`).
- Once an app is installed, its details page shows whether it's set up this way, so it's clear which layout is in use.
- The setting is remembered across future updates of the same app.
- Removing an app installed this way now also offers to clean up its dedicated folder. If the folder only ever contained the app itself, it's removed automatically. If the AppImage left behind its own data in that folder, you're asked whether to keep or delete it.
- Added Arabic translations for all new interface text.

title: Add support for custom app names
body:
Lets you give an integrated app a custom display name that survives updates, closing #160 (and covering #468's per-copy naming for side-by-side versions).

A pencil button next to the app title on the details page (installed apps only) opens a small popover to edit the name; a reset button restores the AppImage's own name. The name is stored as `X-GearLever-CustomName` in the generated `.desktop` file and re-applied whenever the entry is regenerated, so it survives updates (URL updates, "Update all", and "Reload metadata"). Only the `Name=` field changes -- the AppImage, `.desktop` and icon file names on disk are left untouched.

Since the display name can now differ from the AppImage's own name, the already-installed / Keep-or-Replace detection (`is_updatable`, the drag-in replace flow, and `gearlever --integrate`) now matches on `X-AppImage-Name` instead of the display name, so updating a renamed app still replaces it rather than silently installing a duplicate. Kept side-by-side copies keep their own identity.

Deliberately out of scope: no file renaming (that's #77/#135), no exec-argument persistence (#376), and no change to the per-app config format.

Notes:
- Renaming clears any localized `Name[xx]` on the entry so the custom name shows on all locales; reverting restores the AppImage's own default name (localized variants come back on the next "Reload metadata").
- The pencil uses a bundled Adwaita symbolic icon, since `document-edit-symbolic` isn't guaranteed in the runtime icon theme.

title: Feature request: Detect a new modern kind of AppImage
body:
I found out there are efforts to modernize AppImage creation:
https://github.com/VHSgunzo/uruntime
https://github.com/VHSgunzo/sharun
https://github.com/pkgforge-dev/Anylinux-AppImages
https://pkgforge-dev.github.io/Anylinux-AppImages/  
I think it would be nice to support these efforts by specifically detecting them as "Type 3" or "Modern type 2".
You can detect these new appimages by running `--appimage-help`, and it should match (the version field can change)
```
Universal RunImage and AppImage runtime with SquashFS and DwarFS supports v0.5.6
   Repository: https://github.com/VHSgunzo/uruntime
```
There are two types of these new appimages:
```
AnyLinux AppImages (made with sharun)
Use FUSE if available, else fallback to using namespaces and if that is not possible then we automatically extract to TMPDIR and run with post cleanup, we do not need an FHS filesystem and do not depend on the host libc, so eh make sure you have write access to /tmp??? (If you can boot to a graphical session you already met those requirements). How is this possible? See: [How to guide](https://github.com/pkgforge-dev/Anylinux-AppImages/blob/main/HOW-TO-MAKE-THESE.md)

AnyLinux AppImages (made with RunImage)
```

title: Add RemoteDirectoryUpdater for HTTP directory listings
body:
## Summary

Adds a new update manager, **RemoteDirectoryUpdater**, that handles applications distributed through a plain HTTP/HTTPS directory index (Apache/nginx autoindex), where releases are published side by side as versioned files.

Given:
- a **directory URL** (e.g. `https://download.linphone.org/releases/linux/app/`)
- a **file name pattern** containing a `*` wildcard that represents the version part (e.g. `Linphone-*.AppImage` or `Linphone-*-x86_64.AppImage`)

it lists the remote directory, matches every file against the pattern, and selects the **highest version** using a natural version sort (so `5.0.10` correctly ranks above `5.0.9`). The latest matching file is then used for the update.

## Implementation

- `src/models/RemoteDirectoryUpdater.py`: new `UpdateManager` subclass.
  - `fetch_target_asset()` parses the HTML index (extracts `href`s, drops sorting links, parent/sub directories), converts the wildcard pattern to an anchored regex (each `*` becomes a capturing group = version), and picks the max via a natural sort key.
  - Download is delegated to `StaticFileUpdater` (same pattern as the Github/Gitlab/Codeberg/Forgejo updaters).
  - Update detection compares the remote file size (`HEAD`) with the local file size, consistent with the other size-based updaters.
  - Two config fields: `url` + `filename`; `validate_config` enforces an `http(s)://` URL and the presence of a `*`.
- `src/models/UpdateManagerChecker.py`: registered in `get_models()`.

## Testing

Validated the parsing and version-selection logic against the live Linphone index:
- pattern `Linphone-*.AppImage` → 56 matches, latest correctly resolved to `6.1.2`.
- pattern `Linphone-*-x86_64.AppImage` → 5 matches, latest `6.1.2` → `Linphone-6.1.2-x86_64.AppImage`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Desktop entry icons are not showing in Fuzzel
body: ## Issue First of all, thanks for creating and maintaining Gear Lever. It really helps me a lot to organize my AppImages. After using Gear Lever for a while, I noticed the desktop entries that are created by Gear Lever don't show it's icons in [Fuzzel](https://codeberg.org/dnkl/fuzzel) although the desktop entries have correct `Icon` path/value and the icon file exists. Example [ProtonUp-Qt](https://github.com/DavidoTek/ProtonUp-Qt) in Fuzzel ProtonUp-Qt desktop entry ```desktop [Desktop Entry] Type=Application Name=ProtonUp-Qt Comment=Install Wine and Proton-based Compatibility Tools Comment[de]=Wine und Proton Kompatibilitätstools installieren Comment[it]=Installa tool di compatibilità basati su Wine e Proton Comment[nl]=Installeer op Wine en Proton gebaseerde compatibiliteitshulpmiddelen Comment[pl]=Zainstaluj narzędzia kompatybilności oparte na Wine i Protonie Icon=/home/mangkoran/AppImages/.icons/protonupqt TryExec=/home/mangkoran/AppImages/protonupqt.appimage Exec=/home/mangkoran/AppImages/protonupqt.appimage Terminal=false Categories=Game;Utility; X-AppImage-Arch=x86_64 X-AppImage-Version=2.15.0 X-AppImage-Name=ProtonUp-Qt ``` Icon ```sh ❯ eza -lga ~/AppImages/.icons/protonupqt* .rw-r--r-- 21k mangkoran mangkoran 20 Feb 23:02 /home/mangkoran/AppImages/.icons/protonupqt ``` After some investigation, I found that the desktop entry icons will show only if the icon file has the correct file extension. ```sh ❯ cp ~/AppImages/.icons/protonupqt{,.png} ❯ eza -lga ~/AppImages/.icons/protonupqt* .rw-r--r-- 21k mangkoran mangkoran 20 Feb 23:02 /home/mangkoran/AppImages/.icons/protonupqt .rw-r--r-- 21k mangkoran mangkoran 20 Feb 23:02 /home/mangkoran/AppImages/.icons/protonupqt.png ``` Updated ProtonUp-Qt desktop entry ```diff -Icon=/home/mangkoran/AppImages/.icons/protonupqt +Icon=/home/mangkoran/AppImages/.icons/protonupqt.png ``` ProtonUp-Qt in Fuzzel now shows icon Is this behavior (no icon file extension) intended? ## Quick Investigation From my investigation, it seems the AppImage icons are copied to `~/AppImages/.icons` directory in the following lines. https://github.com/mijorus/gearlever/blob/25850448881cebc027572dde4c316e61f0ec1874/src/providers/AppImageProvider.py#L352-L357 However it seems the icon file extension `icon_file_ext` may be missing which caused the copied icon files don't have the correct file extension. Although I haven't checked the behavior in other app launcher other than Fuzzel, it seems icon file extension is expected/preferred based on [Icon Theme Specification](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/icon-theme/latest/#directory_layout) (also applies to desktop entry icons). > The image files must be one of the types: PNG, XPM, or SVG, and the extension must be ".png", ".xpm", or ".svg" (lower case). --- Edit: Tested in Gear Lever 4.4.10 installed from [AUR](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/gearlever). Edit 2: Tested in Gear Lever 4.6.2 Flatpak

title: [Issue] Reloading metadata removes sources and command line arguments
body: As the title suggests, reloading metadata in an app resets it's sources and command line arguments (the latter being an issue since #339). If you provide a source and click **reload metadata**, it changes to `default` which has the outcome of the source you provided being wiped (when you change from `default` to the source you had selected, said source will be gone). ## Possible fix "Reload metadata" current behavior is pretty much a "reset" button. That's fine on it's own, but it should take the following into account: ### 1. Command line arguments If a command line argument was provided, it should remain untouched. If it is empty, it should reset it to whatever is the default. > Directly related to #339 ### 2. Sources If a user provides a valid source to ANY available options (GitHub, Gitlab, Forgejo, etc), that source should be stored. It shouldn't reset by cycling between the available options or from "reload metadata". ^ That way, if you clicked "reload metadata": - With a valid source selected - It should remain unchanged; - With an invalid source - It should reset it and change to `default`; - With an empty source - It should change to `default`. > "Empty source" being a source you had selected (Gitlab, for example), but the fields were empty. ### Screenshots My current settings (using osu! as an example): Reloading metadata (in progress...): Metadata reloaded. It had the following outcome: 1. The sources I provided got wiped and changed to `default`. > If a command line argument was provided, it would also be wiped 2. Changing `default` to the source I was using (`GitHub` in this case); 3. The source I had here is gone. Expected behavior: Since I provided a valid GitHub source, it shouldn't reset it and change to `default`.

title: Proposal: Support for Official, Community, and Local AppImage Lists
body:
Love the program, and it has been extremely useful.

I put a lot of thought into how we can improve the user experience and I believe we can make some great changes while staying true to being a lightweight appimage manager.

### The Current Friction
- We have to manually download and install the appimage
- We can only configure an appimage after adding it
- We can't backup/share our settings
- There is a massive amount of redundant effort as every user is manually entering the exact same update URLs for common software like Obsidian or VLC.

### The Proposal: JSON AppImage Manifests

I propose implementing a JSON schema to define AppImage entries. Ideally, pointing Gear Lever to a JSON definition could automatically handle the download, architecture check, and update path configuration in one go.

Here is a simplified example of what a definition could look like:

```
{
  "name": "Obsidian",
  "architectures": ["x86_64", "aarch64"],
  "tags": ["Office", "Notes"],
  "update": {
    "source_type": "github",
    "repository": "obsidianmd/obsidian-releases",
    "release_patterns": {
      "x86_64": "Obsidian-*-x64.AppImage",
      "aarch64": "Obsidian-*-arm64.AppImage"
    }
  }
}
```
By decoupling the definition from the executable, we open the door to "Lists" or Repositories:

1.  Local Files (Highest Priority): Users can drop files like emulators.json or my_osu_setup.json into ~/.config/gearlever/. This inherently solves the "backup/export" issue and allows for personal execution flags.

2. Community/Personal Lists: Users could add custom repository URLs for curated lists (e.g., a trusted builds list or a specific gaming repository) or their own personal list of programs.

3. Official List: A simple default repository maintained by Gear Lever containing definitions for common tools (browsers, editors).

Here's an example schema that could take one or many app images as input.
[schema.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26523772/schema.txt)

So in my .config folder, I could have an emulators.json, mylist.json, osu.json

### UI Implementation
I propose a simple searchable/filterable collapsible list in the main ui, where users can see this list of available appimages for their arch. With tabs for the custom lists/local files.

Users should be able to select one or more items from the list and install them from the list.

I think this will really make life easier for most users, and reduce the amount of frustration users have in managing their appimages.

While I am not familiar enough with the core codebase to write the backend implementation I would love to help
If you are open to this direction, I can help with UX and UI fitting your constraints, testing, and building and maintaining the repos and documentation. 


I hope this fits within the vision of the program, and I'm hoping for some feedback.

> The following special values are supported:
>
> - `latest`: Automatically detects the latest GitHub Release
> - `latest-pre:` Automatically detects the latest GitHub Prerelease. Useful, e.g., to implement a beta/prerelease update concept.
> - `latest-all`: Automatically detects the latest GitHub Release or Prerelease. Useful if you want prerelease users to automatically switch to a stable release until another prerelease is made.

according to the log, it's putting `latest-all` in the url which is invalid:

title: GitHub update tags other than `latest` don't work.
body:
In `GithubUpdater`'s  `get_url_data`, the update info is parsed, and `url_data["release"]` is set to the tag name.  Then `fetch_target_asset` will fetch info from `https://api.github.com/repos/<username>/<repo>/<release>`. This works for `latest`, but not for anything else. An AppImage set to update from a moving tag that isn't marked latest will fail, because for anything but the latest, the format of the url should instead be `https://api.github.com/repos/<username>/<repo>/tags/<release>`.

It also doesn't seem like `latest-all` and `latest-pre` are being accounted for either.
https://github.com/AppImage/AppImageSpec/blob/master/draft.md#release-name-values

title: Offer more flexibility to match release file names in Updater models
body:
Hello,

This PR aims at fixing #364.
In the example provided with that issue, this PR would allow differentiating the target filename in the release filename:
- `avidemux_*.*.*.appImage` would match `avidemux_2.8.1.appImage`
- `avidemux_*.*.*_legacy.appImage` would match `avidemux_2.8.1_legacy.appImage`

That would nevertheless requires most users to upgrade their configuration. If you wanted to avoid this for at least a certain number of cases, adding the dot to the regex characters class (`[a-zA-Z0-9.]`) may help.

title: Gearlever crashes when calling arch (missing command) → UI stuck on loading

When attempting to integrate an AppImage with Gearlever, the application crashes because it tries to execute the command arch, which is not available on all systems. As a result, the UI remains stuck indefinitely in the “loading” state.

Gearlever currently uses:

`system_arch = sandbox_sh(['arch'])`

in [AppDetails.py](https://github.com/mijorus/gearlever/blob/master/src/AppDetails.py)


However I was able to fix the issue locally by replacing it with :

`system_arch = sandbox_sh(['uname', '-m'])`

title: Usability questions and suggestions
body:
Hi, there.

I have been looking for a simple app to manage AppImages for a while, basically an app that would provide a simple way to integrate them to the app list (create the proper .desktop file) without running a background service, and found Gear Lever recently. I really liked:

- nice UI
- can open downloaded files with double click
- create/remove the .desktop file with a click
- keep all AppImage files organized in a single place

Here are some points that may be improved, at least in my opinion:

1. Is there any special reason why the AppImage file is renamed when "installed" (i.e. moved to the chosen folder and the .desktop file created)? Retaining the name helps with some things, like searching for the same file online later, or even just for keeping the proper record (the file name may contain the version, for instance).
2. Why it uses [TryExec](https://github.com/mijorus/gearlever/blob/69f405a8dad8ff83d6180c3e63b570833529f119/src/providers/AppImageProvider.py#L103) instead of just Exec to detect other installed app images? Just wondering... I had some AppImages with the proper desktop files and Gear Lever did not detect any of them out of the box.
3. Maybe Reload Metadata should be disabled for apps that were not "installed" with Gear Lever? Or, at least, if it created a new .desktop file then also delete the old one? Personally, I think it would safer (and simpler) if this was disabled for "external" AppImages.
4. When using the "+Open" button to add a new AppImage, filter by "AppImage/appimage" by default, with the option to "show all files" as option.
5. It seems that Gear Lever creates a file "apps.json" in ~/.config, right? I am very glad that it did not create a new dot file in the home directory, but it would be much better if it used XDG standards and created the file in something like $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/it.mijorus.gearlever or just $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/gearlever instead (if XDG_CONFIG_HOME does not exist, then default to ~/.config). To avoid update problems, then the app could check if it exists there first, if not then use the current location so this will not cause problem when users update the app.


Please feel free to ask for more info if needed, or to open separated issues for each item above.

Thanks again! Regards

title: GitHub API Rate Limit Silently Fails Updates; Feature: User Notification & API Token Support
body:
### Problem: GitHub API Rate Limiting Leads to Misleading "No Updates" Message

When Gear Lever attempts to automatically update AppImages using GitHub release links (e.g., `https://api.github.com/repos/xpipe-io/xpipe/releases/latest`), it can encounter GitHub API rate limiting. This is typically observed when making numerous requests within a short period.

**Current Behavior:**

Upon encountering a GitHub API rate limit, Gear Lever logs a `403 Client Error: rate limit exceeded`:

```
2025-07-08 09:23:19,020 ERROR [UpdateManager.py:376] 403 Client Error: rate limit exceeded for url: https://api.github.com/repos/xpipe-io/xpipe/releases/latest
```

However, this error is not communicated to the user. Instead, Gear Lever displays a "No updates available" message, which is incorrect and misleading. The user is left unaware that an attempt was made and failed due to external limitations, rather than an actual absence of updates.

**Impact:**

*   Users are not informed about critical update failures.
*   Users might mistakenly believe their AppImages are up-to-date when they are not.
*   Debugging update issues becomes more challenging for users.

### Proposed Solutions: Enhancing Robustness and User Experience

To address this bug and improve the reliability of updates, I propose two inter-related enhancements:

#### 1. Bug Fix: Notify User of Rate Limit Errors

**Request:** When Gear Lever encounters a GitHub API rate limit (HTTP 403 with a rate limit message), it should clearly inform the user.

**Possible Implementations:**

*   **Dedicated User Interface Notification:** A pop-up, status bar message, or a clear indicator within the update status area stating something like: "Update check failed for some AppImages due to GitHub API rate limiting. Please try again later, or consider adding a GitHub API token."
*   **Detailed Log Message (User-facing):** While not a primary UI notification, ensuring the log provides more user-friendly guidance.

#### 2. Feature Request: Allow User to Provide a GitHub API Token

**Request:** Implement an option within Gear Lever's settings to allow users to provide a personal GitHub API token. This token would be used for authenticated requests to the GitHub API, significantly increasing the rate limit and largely bypassing this issue for active users.

**Benefits:**

*   **Bypass Rate Limits:** Authenticated requests have a much higher rate limit (5000 requests per hour) compared to unauthenticated requests (60 requests per hour for the same IP).
*   **Improved Reliability:** Users with many AppImages or those who frequently check for updates would experience fewer "phantom" update failures.
*   **Empowers Power Users:** Gives advanced users control over their update experience.

**Considerations for API Token Implementation:**

*   **Security:** The API token must be stored securely (e.g., encrypted) and never exposed in cleartext.
*   **User Interface:** A clear input field in settings, perhaps with a link to GitHub's documentation on generating personal access tokens.
*   **Scope:** The token would ideally only require the `public_repo` scope or no specific scopes for public repository information (but `public_repo` is often easiest to recommend to users).
*   **Validation:** Basic validation of the token upon entry or first use.

title: #83 AppImage generation with docker
body:
Refer to discussion at:
https://github.com/mijorus/gearlever/issues/83#issuecomment-2889022248

This is a heavy prototype that get's its job done, at least as far as I am aware. I created it with a heavy help from the copilot, because in the topic of appimages, I know very little. The commands in the RUN are left in a debug format because I have been tinkering with them and adding/removing each one, so that I needed new layers. For final build it must be adjusted, of course.

**It is a DRAFT, meant to be further distilled into a proper contribution with the help of others.**

Right now the .dockerignore and the github workflow is generated and I didn't even check if it is sensible.

The docker image, however, *works* and produces runnable AppImage. To test it:
```
docker build -t gearlever-appimage -f .docker/Dockerfile .
docker run --volume ./build:/host:rw gearlever-image
```
and you should have a built artifact inside the `/build` directory on your machine.

Copying from my earlier comment, what's left to do is:

1. verify that it works for others
2. verify that the generated appimage is correct and has everything it needs in correct places
3. clean up the current docker process (it is written in a debug-friendly way but probably very suboptimal for real use case)
4. write github action to automate building the appimage
5. in the matter of future work, expand with features meant to integrate the app image into the system. AFAIK there are 2 things right now which need to be supported:   
   - install and move the gear lever itself to it's own managed directory
   - make sure auto-updates work
   
   
Regarding the packages installed in the docker: 
- It has this weird format because I tried using local cache to avoid constant pull when I was working on the package list.
- I don't know if this package list is proper. I have generated the initial list with the help of copilot by prompting it to read the whole repository. Then I've been stepping through the build process, finding what's broken and installing missing ones. If someone could confirm what's needed/what's not, I would be helpful.
- I don't know how appmimages work internally, and if they do/should bundle certain packages or not. I looked through several threads and read that for common (i.e. expected) packages it is not needed (e.g. python3), and for others I don't know

title: AppImage update URL is forced to incorrect package for Zen Twilight
body:
Currently using Zen browser and ran into an issue where all tabs would crash on certain links being opened, issue has been fixed in Zen Twilight so I have started to use that: https://zen-browser.app/download/?twilight
But when I download and open the Twilight AppImage in Gearlever, unlocking and moving the file automatically sets the Github URL with asterisks defined for the normal Zen AppImage.

Normal Zen github links use the version number for the release naming:
https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/releases/download/*/zen-x86_64.AppImage.zsync

But Twilight release just uses the Twilight tag release for all releases, should be:
https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/releases/download/twilight/zen-x86_64.AppImage.zsync

Because the twilight app is forced to use the normal apps update URL, it will think there is a new update and will just fail with this error if you try to update it:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8ecd5322-d5e1-4dfb-b280-6564e991010a)

For github links is gearlever just scanning for new filenames or releases, or does it check hashes to see if there is a new version as well? I wanted to just add the twilight link as a static URL but cannot due to the URL dropdown box being greyed out and the github link being uneditable.

title: Improve launch options for AppImage desktop integration, especially during AppImage updates.
body:
Currently with the current AppImage integration programs (Gear Lever, AppImage Launcher and others) there is a very annoying issue, when you update an AppImage also overwrites the . desktop file that is automatically generated in $HOME/. local/share/applications without the user’s consent, so any changes to the launch options on the .desktop file made by the user will be lost and the user will have to re-add them manually.

This is a problem for those looking to start another program along with the AppImage, such as using mangohud on OpenGL applications (the MANGOHUD environment variable only works with Vulkan applications) and/or want to use firejail to confine an AppImage, as the current launch options setting in Gear Lever is only for running launch arguments after the AppImage has been launched.

This could be implemented in several ways, but the ones I'm thinking about right now are:

- Add another launch options box that runs before the application and allow custom launch options to persist after updates 
- Alternatively a confirmation checkbox option (per app) to prevent the. desktop file to be overwritten when updating the AppImage from Gear Lever

I hope I've been able to explain myself well, English is not my native language. :P

title: Error with Update URL for Warp Terminal AppImage
body:
### Issue Description
According to Gear Lever's documentation, it supports both static URLs and GitHub releases for specifying AppImage update URLs. I have attempted to add an update URL for Warp Terminal using the Gear Lever interface. The URL I provided (`https://app.warp.dev/get_warp?package=appimage`) redirects to the latest version of the Warp Terminal AppImage, currently located at `https://releases.warp.dev/stable/v0.2025.02.12.16.51.stable_03/Warp-x86_64.AppImage`.

### Error Encountered
Gear Lever is throwing an error when I enter this update URL. It seems that Gear Lever might expect a direct URL to the AppImage file instead of a URL that redirects to the latest version. 

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8a138412-1b05-46b3-a4d8-66fddb73aa15)

### Expected Behavior
Gear Lever should support update URLs that redirect to the latest version of the AppImage file, as long as it conforms to the expected format for update URLs.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Add an application using Gear Lever.
2. Enter the update URL `https://app.warp.dev/get_warp?package=appimage`.
3. Observe the error thrown by Gear Lever related to the update URL.

### Additional Information
- Gear Lever version: 3.0.1
- Operating System: SteamOS 3.6.21

Please advise on how to correctly configure the update URL or if there are any specific requirements for URLs in Gear Lever that I might have missed.

I'm unsure whether this is an issue in the libreoffice appimage but it does not seem critical to the function of gearlever or libreoffice so continuing and logging the error for future reference seemed appropriate.

title: About the unofficial AppImage
body:
Ciao Lorenzo,

I have seen you have published the link to my build on your README.

Well, if you want to do so, please specify that it is just a "proof of concept", since it is not 100% working as it should.

When I create AppImages, I use the more accessible base that upstream or third-party provides. In this case, the base is the unofficial AUR package, that in my opninion, deserve more visibility than my release: since its was built to work on Arch Linux out of the box, mine is just a test I'm doing.

In my projects, I use three different ways to build AppImages:
- [Archimage](https://github.com/ivan-hc/ArchImage), uses Arch Linux packages, also from AUR. They are Arch Linux containers into AppImages, and to work they rely on their own resources. The main part of my projects are based on it ([VirtualBox](https://github.com/ivan-hc/VirtualBox-appimage), [Gnome Boxes](https://github.com/ivan-hc/Boxes-appimage), [OBS Studio](https://github.com/ivan-hc/OBS-Studio-appimage), [VLC](https://github.com/ivan-hc/VLC-appimage), [GIMP](https://github.com/ivan-hc/GIMP-appimage), [Bottles](https://github.com/ivan-hc/Bottles-appimage)...). Also Gear Lever has this base.
- [AppImaGen](https://github.com/ivan-hc/AppImaGen), it uses DEB packages, or even TAR/ZIP archives. Among my methods, this is what is more similar to the standard ones.
- [Snap2AppImage](https://github.com/ivan-hc/Snap2AppImage), converts Snap packages to AppImages. It is perfect for Electron apps and Chromium-based programs (my [Skype](https://github.com/ivan-hc/Skype-appimage) and [Chromium](https://github.com/ivan-hc/Chromium-Web-Browser-appimage) are examples)

Archimage is my favourite one, but if I have so many AppImages with different bases its because each method has its limits. And Archimage is not a good method to build Gear Lever. AppImaGen would be.

For now, I noticed my Archimage of Gear Lever can only integrate AppImages in the menu and launch "some" AppImages, not all. Archimages cannot be launched, since Gear Lever itself is an Archimage, so trying to launch JuNest with JuNest gives this error
```
Error: Nested JuNest environments are not allowed
```
Also, some AppImages (in general) still need host libraries, and since Gear Lever works into an Arch Linux container, normal AppImages will rely on what is already in Gear Lever. This should not be a problem for the Flatpak, since it has its big runtimes... but for a small Archimage it means to bloat the package with libraries that Gear Lever does not need.

Also, this is still experimental, and this night, to made it even smaller and[ fix workflows that were failing from more than one month](https://github.com/ivan-hc/Database-of-pkg2appimaged-packages/actions/workflows/gearlever.yml) (the issue was the transiction from python3.12 to 3.13 in Arch, that was putting the "mesonbuild" module in the wrong directory) I lost the ability of updating the AppImages, that indeed was present in my previous build (it's almost 8am now, I'll try to fix it later...maybe).

That said, I'm puttin too much effort in this experimental project and I'm planning to remove it from my package manager AM because it is still too much buggy.

If you want a working AppImage made by me, please provide a portable bundle or a DEB package, I'll take care of the rest.

Also, there are still other issues opened by @probonopd that wanted to help you by using its experience, being him the creator of the AppImage package format.

People who want to help you are a lot. I'm part of a community (pkgforge) that also works on other methods to package programs in a portable way.

But please, don't delegate things that are not my responsibility. The AppImage I AM TRYING TO CREATE is just for demonstration purposes, and to help you understand how AppImages work, because they are anything but packages to be extracted with 7zip: they have their own method to be extracted, even without FUSE, and they can very well be isolated or closed in a sandbox. I know this well. I have my own AppImage package manager that I have been working on for over three years now, "AM". I have no intention of taking credit or demerits for a package that is not ready, and that people might want to download just because the real upstream developer published it on the README.

Best regards... e forza Napoli!

title: Feature request: Prepend arguments to the run command
body:
> When I say "run command" I'm referring to the command that is executed when an appimage is started through gearlever.

Hello, I love your program and use it daily. There is however one feature that I feel is lacking, and that is the ability to prepend arguments/commands to the run command. This can be useful when you are running games and want to use a wrapper such as Mangohud or Gamemode.
The ideal implementation would probably be something like the way steam does it, using a %command% or %appimage% shorthand containing the appimage path. So if you were to set the command line arguments to `mangohud %command% --foo --bar` and the path to the appimage was `/usr/progam.appimage` then the executed command would be `mangohud /usr/program.appimage --foo --bar`.

body:
I installed gear lever from flathub to create a shortcut to ente's auth.appimage v4.0.2 on NixOS and make it work. with gear lever I made auth.appimage executable and a shortcut was created. i clicked on the shortcut, it didn't work. 

I followed the steps in the manual to run appimage in NixOS. manual URL:
https://nixos.org/manual/nixos/stable/#sec-custom-packages-prebuilt

To run appimage on NixOS you need to install the appimage-run package. Then you run a console in the directory of the appimage file. Then run it with the command:
`appimage-run ./auth.appimage`
or console anywhere:
`appimage-run auth.appimage`
and run it.

normally in other classic gnu/linux distributions 
`chmod +x auth.appimage`
`./auth.appimage`
commands. But it's different in NixOS. So in the .desktop file of appimage, appimage-run is added to the Exec= line. 
`Exec=appimage-run /appimage_file_location/auth.appimage`
It didn't work even though I added it. Normally zen-browser.appimage appimage-run zen-browser.appimage worked. But when I changed the `Exec=` line in zen-browser.desktop it didn't work. 

For more detailed information on the subject:
https://github.com/ente-io/ente/issues/3795

then i changed the content of the shortcut file auth.desktop. I changed
`Exec=/home/macellan/AppImages/auth. appimage ente_auth %u`
to
`Exec=appimage-run /home/macellan/AppImages/auth.appimage ente_auth %u`
and saved it. then entered the command `chmod +x auth.desktop`. then tried to run it, `./auth.desktop` didn't work. clicked on the shortcut, didn't work.
I changed `Exec=appimage-run .....` in the zen-browser.desktop file of the zen-browser shortcut I created with gear lever. I clicked on the shortcut. zen-browser didn't work either. whereas appimage-run worked with the zen-browser.appimage command.
finally I ran console in auth.appimage directory. followed by `chmod +x auth.appimage`: `./auth.appimage` and again it didn't work.

Anyway...
The point is that gear lever does not run appimage files on NixOS. When I click on the “Start” button of the app I want to run in the Gear Lever app, it doesn't start. Because it doesn't run directly in NixOS. Necessary changes need to be made in the .desktop file. The changes that need to be made are related to `appimage-run`. But I have no idea where and what kind of changes need to be made. Maybe a correct change in the `Exec=` line in the .desktop file would be enough. 
The gear lever app should also do this configuration and .desktop shortcut file creation for NixOS. For NixOS this application needs to be modified and updated.

Code lines should be added to the application for NixOS and updated, and the current version should be published. Best regards.

title: Add option to run the AppImage with firejail sandbox.
body:
AppImage is a bundling format that compared to alternatives (Flatpak, Snap) does not impose any restriction for running program to the resources on the host (user home, services on dbus, network, etc.) apart from the obvious restriction that linux processes have given their global uid/gid and in some other cases as SELinux/Apparmor - nothing beyond what Linux distribution provides.

As many of the software provided as AppImages are proprietary (arguable it's more popular for distributing proprietary software than Flatpak) and for increasing runtime security for open source apps I find myself running AppImages with firejail.

[firejail](https://firejail.wordpress.com/) a versatile sandboxing solution for binaries on Linux that uses the underlying kernel technologies in similar vein to container runtimes. I'm using this setup all the time and  find myself running (in this case to have a private home directory and restrictions on dbus services access):
```
> firejail --private --nodbus --appimage <some-appimage>
```

Over the years there have been discussions and some proposed solution to streamline firejail-ing appimages, for example here - [discourse thread](https://discourse.appimage.org/t/new-appimaged-optional-daemon-that-registers-appimages-with-the-system/87) and here - [another  thread](https://discourse.appimage.org/t/deeper-integration-with-firejail-for-sandboxing/88).

I propose to add that functionality within GearLever. As firejail has plethora of cli options controlling separation from host for different resources I think that user should be given the option to construct cli themselves. That's a general enough solution to encompass any possible "wrapper" for the appimage file - for ease of use for the firejail usecase a template can be provided that user can start with.

title: Duplicate entries in menu
body:
When adding an app image without the option `Use executable name for integrated terminal apps` and moving the file to the application folder, Gear Lever creates a desktop file with the long name (example `gearlever_fritzing_1a993c.desktop`).

If the app image is removed from the folder via the file manager and not Gear Lever, the desktop file remains. If the app image is again imported but with the previously mentioned option enabled, a new desktop file is created and Gear Lever shows the same applications twice. Removing the application via the menu or via the file manager removes both entries, the only way to fix it was to remove the offending desktop file.

(And a quick way to find it was `find / -name "$NAME_OF_APPLICATION" -type f 2>/dev/null`.)

title: AppImage type detection wrong
body:
As per the [AppImageSpec](https://github.com/AppImage/AppImageSpec/blob/fb05d9e1b8b8616dbeb7491303edc537dca573f3/draft.md#image-format), currently there are only two _image formats_: Types 1 and 2.

* Type 1 can be identified by checking for the magic hex `0x414901` at offset 8.
* Type 2 can be identified by checking for the magic hex `0x414902` at offset 8.

So why is this talking about a type 3 then?

Also, the types exist as alternatives, and they are not called "generation".

https://github.com/mijorus/gearlever/blob/3702f37b0e2e35d0fe516d15121c7081da9a19ed/src/providers/AppImageProvider.py#L466-L481

The fix would be something like this (untested):

```
def get_appimage_type(self, el: AppImageListElement) -> int:
    file = Gio.File.new_for_path(el.file_path)
    try:
        with open(file.get_path(), 'rb') as f:
            magic = f.read(4)
            if magic == b'\x41\x49\x01':  # 0x414901
                type = 1
            elif magic == b'\x41\x49\x02':  # 0x414902
                type  = 2
      except Exception as e:
          type = 0

    return type
```

Related:
* https://github.com/ivan-hc/AM/issues/818

title: Issues with updater if ARM filenames have suffix, while x64 filenames don't
body:
Hello. I've encountered an issue with the GitHub updater on a few repos that release their ARM AppImages with suffix, but their x64 AppImages without a suffix; similar to this:
- AppName-1.0.0.AppImage
- AppName-1.0.0-arm64.AppImage

This causes Gear Lever to both incorrectly assume there's an update and potentially download an AppImage for the wrong architecture. This occurs, for example, with [Kopia](https://github.com/kopia/kopia):
```
2024-07-11 15:00:59,839 INFO [AppImageProvider.py:263] Installing appimage: /var/home/ethan/Downloads/KopiaUI-0.17.0.AppImage
...
2024-07-11 15:09:07,072 INFO [UpdateManager.py:132] Downloading file from https://github.com/kopia/kopia/releases/download/v0.17.0/KopiaUI-0.17.0-arm64.AppImage
```

I believe the best solution for this would be to first check for URLs where all wildcards (`*`) match:
1. Update URL is set to `https://github.com/kopia/kopia/releases/download/v*/KopiaUI-*.AppImage`
2. Gear Lever checks for the latest **tag name**, which would be `v0.17.0` (with a `v`) at time of posting
3. Gear Lever determines that the `*` matches `0.17.0` (**without the `v`**)
4. Gear Lever checks for the existence of `https://github.com/.../v0.17.0/KopiaUI-0.17.0.AppImage`
5. Gear Lever finds the file and uses it to update

Or, if it doesn't find the file, it proceeds with the previous logic.

title: Update appdata according to the freedesktop appstream specifications, fix homepage url, switch to appstreamcli
body:
The url in the appdata.xml doesn't seem to be reachable, possibly because it doesn't auto-complete to adding a "/" on the end of the link whereas a web browser does. 

```
W: it.mijorus.gearlever:7: url-not-reachable
     https://mijorus.it/projects/gearlever - Unexpected status code: 301
   Unable to reach remote location that this URL references - does it exist?
```

Simply adding a / on the end allows the link to be reachable.

The <developer_name> tag has been deprecated according to the [freedesktop appstream specifications](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/appstream/docs/chap-Metadata.html#tag-developer). I updated to the \<developer> tag instead, made it untranslatable and use a unique id of "it.mijorus".

I believe flatpak switched to libappstream which uses `appstreamcli validate` instead of appstream-glib's `appstream-util validate` because appstream-glib is deprecated. I switched the check inside meson.build according to this which also allows a `meson test` to succeed. Also added `--no-net` to allow for offline validation, could possibly use `--explain` to allow for a more detailed explanation of any errors but it may not be needed.

title: Allow override for StartupWMClass
body: It would be helpful if you can manually specify the StartupWMClass for the generated `.desktop` file. The reason being that a lot of AppImages unfortunately have the wrong value set, causing icons to be missing on Wayland specifically. It is possible to edit the `.desktop` file manually later, but whenever you refresh the meta information (for example after an update) you end up with messed up icons again.

title: Produce an error log if libfuse is not installed
body:
Currently, if gtk-launch tries to launch the .desktop that points to an app image without fuse installed, the gtk-launch returns 0 which does not trigger an exception even if the app image returns a non-zero code. Though, if ran through gearlever without installing the app image first (skipping gtk-launch and running the app image directly), an error is still not logged through the exception in host_sh. 

I leveraged the callback feature provided in host_threaded_sh, run the callback through log_command_output to write an error log to the file but only if fuse is not installed: 
`ERROR [utils.py:160] dlopen(): error loading libfuse.so.2AppImages require FUSE to run. You might still be able to extract the contents of this AppImage if you run it with the --appimage-extract option. See https://github.com/AppImage/AppImageKit/wiki/FUSE for more information`

I filtered and only logged the libfuse error because app images could bloat the log file with their own errors not related to the functioning of gearlever itself. Hopefully this change provides some indication for users as to why their app images won't launch.

title: Add a check to avoid copying the demo.AppImage file multiple times
body:
The welcome screen checks if the path to the demo.AppImage file in the user's cache directory exists but not if the demo file itself exists. 

To avoid copying the demo file multiple times, I rolled both in to one check (if the file exists then the path to it exists so we can skip both making the directories and copying the file). As well as using `os.makedirs(... exist_ok=True)` to skip making the directories if it exists inside this check without the need to use an additional if statement. 

I also added in `os.path.join()` to my demo_app_dest variable so I changed those around this part for consistency.

title: Consider releasing an AppImage version of GearLever
body: I consider the absence of an AppImage version for Gear Lever and its reliance on Flatpak to be an egregious error. Please don't take offense, but as a Linux user, I strongly dislike the unnecessary clutter caused by Flatpak, Snap, and Java – they consume resources needlessly, and their background processes remain opaque to users. Flatpak and Snap seem like makeshift solutions tailored for former Windows users who migrated to Ubuntu to avoid Microsoft's system charges. The developers behind this decision are reminiscent of Canonical, which altered Debian into something unrecognizable without bothering to consult the documentation, merely patching it to mimic Windows. title: Consider changing ~/AppImages location to ~/.AppImages
body:
Reason?

Visible folders in home should be populated by folders with media & documents (Documents, Downloads, Music, Pictures, Videos etc.)
While invisible files & folders contain configurations, data used by system or apps. They also can include portable app binaries, which AppImages are.

This will make separation between them cleaner.

title: Suggestion: do not delete appimage upon remove
body: When removing an app it will also delete the original appimage file. Perhaps a better behavior (or maybe a preference option) will be to rename the appimage file back to it's original name without the "gearlever" prefix.

title: Install icons to XDG_DATA_DIRS and include file extensions
body: Currently, the icons are installed to `~/AppImages/.icons/gearlever_[app name]_[md5]`, without a file extension. I believe this is undesirable because some applications don't support choosing icon by path, and some don't work with icons without explicit file extension. It would be helpful if the icons were installed to the canonical location of `$prefix/share/icons/hicolor/[size]/apps` (e.g. `~/.local/share/icons/hicolor/512x512/apps`), and if the file extension (usually .png) is included, per [XDG spec](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/icon-theme-spec/icon-theme-spec-latest.html).

title: Run AppImages in Portable Mode
body:
**Feature Request:**
I learned a neat new thing about AppImages today. They can run in portable mode. I like that, because it makes it easier to know where an app keeps its /config and store data it uses. I would like Gearlever to take advanges of this and let the user use this with ease when installing by having Gearlever making the needed folders when "installing" this appimage if they chooses to.

**How:**
If you create a directory named appimagefilename.home in the same directory as the appimage file, it'll treat it as the home directory.

E.g. EmulationStation-DE-x64.AppImage.home

Same applies to config, you can create a directory named something like EmulationStation-DE-x64.AppImage.config

**Docs:**
https://docs.appimage.org/user-guide/portable-mode.html

I tried integrating UpNote image app via Gear Lever on my old laptop running Rhino Linux - Ubuntu based - and the web clipping worked as on Windows (dual boot with Fedora on my new desktop pc). Then I uninstalled Gear Lever in Fedora's Software app, downloaded and installed the rpm package of AppImageLauncher and used it for integrating and launching UpNote app image.
